Alaska.Ai — The Stack Draft

2026-06-04 · branch claude/linkedin-stack-2026-06-04
No defensible target this cycle.
The anti-confabulation gate cleared zero mechanisms in both the 14-day and 21-day windows. No post or image was generated. The run completed correctly.

Mapper Validation Note

14-day window (May 21 – June 4, 2026) was evaluated in full. All eight candidates were assessed. Zero mechanisms survived all seven gates. A 21-day broadening retry (May 14 – June 4) was also evaluated: the only candidate that would move inside the broadened window (C4, Oklo earnings call May 13) remains one day outside even the 21-day window (May 14 cutoff), and in any case fails Gate 3 because every layer's primary source URL returned 403, 404, 503, or cert error during live WebFetch verification. No Gate 5 asymmetric chokepoint was confirmed for the two most advanced candidates (C2: FERC Commission is a 5-member majority-vote body per 42 U.S.C. § 7171, no single commissioner is structurally decisive; C5: named a 'dual gate' by the scout — both RCA 5-member commission and Alaska Legislature are co-equal FID conditions, neither is a single-actor binary chokepoint). Honest no-target result; bar was not lowered.

The FERC early works NTP was filed February 2026, outside the window. An in-window news article triggering the regulatory mechanism was not confirmed. FERC Section 3 NGA Environmental Assessment Gate — Kenai LNG Cool Down Expansion (CP26-61-000)gate_5_failed gate_5_failed — the named chokepoint is the FERC Commission vote (Section 3 NGA authorization order). Per 42 U.S.C. § 7171, the FERC Commission consists of five members and actions are determined by majority vote; no single commissioner is structurally decisive. No alternative single-actor binary decision point was confirmed within the mechanism. Layer 1 primary source (tankterminals.com) returned HTTP 404 during live verification, creating an additional gate_3 failure. The Federal Register notice (May 20, 2026, docket CP26-61-000) confirms the EA schedule but identifies only 'Commission staff' as the EA preparer with no named single official holding binary authority.
Cook Inlet Gas Supply Replenishment Stack — Glenfarne FID / RCA-Legislature Dual Gategate_5_failed gate_5_failed — the mechanism is explicitly structured as a 'dual gate' with two co-equal FID conditions: (1) RCA approval of the Enstar gas purchase agreement and (2) Alaska Legislature passage of a favorable tax agreement. The RCA is a 5-member commission voting by majority; no single RCA officer has binary authority. The Legislature requires passage through both chambers plus the Governor's signature; no single actor controls the binary. Additionally, gate_3 fails for Layer 4: the RCA docket for the Glenfarne-Enstar gas purchase agreement was not confirmed (no docket number found; article states the agreement is 'still being finalized'). Gate_4 is also questionable: the ADN news article contains no mention of AI or data centers; the Alaska AI industry consequence is inferential.
Oklo Aurora Powerhouse — Eielson AFB Microreactor Cogeneration Stackgate_1_failed gate_3_failed gate_1_failed and gate_3_failed — the Oklo Q1 2026 earnings call transcript was published May 13, 2026, which is outside the 14-day window (May 21 – June 4) and also outside the 21-day broadened window (May 14 cutoff; May 13 is 1 day before the 21-day boundary). Under a 21-day broadening retry, gate_3 independently fails: every per-layer primary source URL tested via WebFetch failed (AF.mil 403, DLA.mil 403, defense.gov 403, Air Force Magazine 503, NRC.gov Part 57 page 404, NRC.gov Oklo page confirmed only the denied 2022 application with no new Part 57 COLA docket confirmed, GVEA.com 403). Layer 3 (NRC Part 57 COLA) describes an anticipated future filing, not an existing regulatory proceeding, and therefore has no primary source.

Editor's Note

Run summary: All four scouts ran successfully and returned candidates. The mapper evaluated 8 candidates (2 facilities, 2 vehicles, 3 regulatory, 3 capital_sovereignty — with 2 overlapping the DAF EUL across scouts). The 21-day window broadening was attempted within the mapper run; no additional survivors emerged.

Recurring structural blocker: Alaska energy infrastructure mechanisms in this cycle consistently resolved to multi-member regulatory bodies (FERC Commission, RCA 5-member commission, Alaska Legislature) as their chokepoints, failing Gate 5. The Kenai LNG Cool Down Expansion (CP26-61-000) and Glenfarne FID were the two most-developed candidates and both were dropped on Gate 5.

Near-miss for next cycle: The Oklo Aurora Powerhouse / Eielson AFB microreactor mechanism (NRC Part 57 COLA chokepoint, DLA Energy NOITA) is 1 day outside the 21-day window and had Gate 3 failures due to government site 403/503 blocks. If Oklo publishes Q2 earnings or an NRC filing in the next 1-2 weeks, this mechanism may clear both gates. Scouts should re-check AF.mil and NRC.gov accessibility and look for any post-June 4 announcement about the Part 57 COLA submission.

DAF EUL award: The AFCEC source selection for the 3-base AI data center lease is now in active evaluation post-May 29 deadline. Any coverage of a lease award announcement would be a clean in-window trigger for a future run framed on the AFCEC selection gate (distinct from the May 20 RCA/utility anatomy).

Deviations: None. Standard run. No subagent stalls. No image generated (no-target). No score report generated (no-target). Gmail draft built manually without gmail_draft.py (that script requires a post and image; neither exists in a no-target run).
